detail.body:
# What does this PR do ?

Rescales `global_batch_size` from 192 to 768 in the 256-GPU BF16 NemotronH-56B recipes (`b200` and `gb300`), matching their FP8-CS counterpart recipes and satisfying DP=128 batch divisibility.

# Changelog

- Wrapped `nemotronh_56b_pretrain_64gpu_b200_fp8cs_config()` in `nemotronh_56b_pretrain_256gpu_b200_bf16_config` with `_with_global_batch_size(..., 768)`.
- Wrapped `nemotronh_56b_pretrain_64gpu_gb300_fp8cs_config()` in `nemotronh_56b_pretrain_256gpu_gb300_bf16_config` with `_with_global_batch_size(..., 768)`.
- Added unit tests in `tests/unit_tests/recipes/test_nemotronh_56b_perf_recipes.py` verifying `global_batch_size == 768` and batch divisibility at DP=128.

# GitHub Actions CI

See the [CI section](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-running-github-ci) in the Contributing doc for how to trigger the CI. A Nvidia developer will need to approve and trigger the CI for external contributors.

# Before your PR is "Ready for review"

**Pre checks**:

- [x] Make sure you read and followed [Contributor guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] Did you write any new necessary tests?
- [ ] Did you add or update any necessary documentation?
- [ ] Does the PR affect components that are optional to install? (Ex: Numba, Pynini, Apex etc)
  - [ ] Reviewer: Does the PR have correct import guards for all optional libraries?

# Additional Information

- Related to #6024

# Runtime validation status

The GBS change resolves the DP=128 batch-divisibility failure. A separate retest on Bridge `ea5dded83078` with the equivalent GBS=768 change and MCore `f6c33bde4cdc` reported that B200 BF16 still runs out of GPU memory during a Mamba chunk-state allocation, before the first iteration completes or CUDA-graph capture starts ([details](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/pull/6091#issuecomment-5763717719)). This PR has not been shown to make the 256-GPU BF16 workload runnable end to end. The reported 64-GPU FP8-CS control completed 30 steps; it does not validate the BF16 preset.

The retest confirmed `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` was active. Rank 6 failed a 512 MiB Mamba chunk-state allocation with 119 MiB free; its exit-time peaks were 172.4454 GiB allocated and 173.4551 GiB reserved. The 953.90 MiB reserved-but-unallocated figure means the diagnostic alone cannot distinguish raw capacity from fragmentation or allocation-reuse constraints. Any memory change still requires a 256-GPU BF16 run through steady-state steps. No memory or convergence settings are changed here.

+"""Unit tests for NemotronH 56B 256-GPU performance recipes."""
+
+import pytest
+
+from megatron.bridge.perf_recipes.nemotronh.b200.nemotronh import (
+    nemotronh_56b_pretrain_256gpu_b200_bf16_config,
+    nemotronh_56b_pretrain_256gpu_b200_fp8cs_config,
+)
+from megatron.bridge.perf_recipes.nemotronh.gb300.nemotronh import (
+    nemotronh_56b_pretrain_256gpu_gb300_bf16_config,
+    nemotronh_56b_pretrain_256gpu_gb300_fp8cs_config,
+)
+
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("bf16_factory", "fp8cs_factory"),
+    [
+        (nemotronh_56b_pretrain_256gpu_b200_bf16_config, nemotronh_56b_pretrain_256gpu_b200_fp8cs_config),
+        (nemotronh_56b_pretrain_256gpu_gb300_bf16_config, nemotronh_56b_pretrain_256gpu_gb300_fp8cs_config),
+    ],
+)
+def test_nemotronh_56b_256gpu_bf16_global_batch_size(bf16_factory, fp8cs_factory):
+    """256-GPU BF16 configs rescale global_batch_size to 768, matching FP8-CS and satisfying DP divisibility."""
+    bf16_cfg = bf16_factory()
+    fp8cs_cfg = fp8cs_factory()
+
+    assert bf16_cfg.train.global_batch_size == 768
+    assert bf16_cfg.train.global_batch_size == fp8cs_cfg.train.global_batch_size
+
+    tp = bf16_cfg.model.tensor_model_parallel_size
+    pp = bf16_cfg.model.pipeline_model_parallel_size
+    cp = bf16_cfg.model.context_parallel_size
+    dp = 256 // (tp * pp * cp)
+    mbs = bf16_cfg.train.micro_batch_size
+
+    assert dp == 128
+    assert bf16_cfg.train.global_batch_size % (mbs * dp) == 0

issue_comments.body:
Retested against Bridge main ea5dded83078 and matching MCore f6c33bde4cdc, with the equivalent GBS=768 fix.

B200 and GB300 factory checks pass, confirming six microbatches with TP2, DP128 and MBS1.

The 256-GPU B200 BF16 configuration still OOMs before completing its first iteration or reaching CUDA-graph capture. Configuration and optimizer initialization succeed; the failure occurs during a Mamba chunk-state allocation.

The 64-GPU FP8-CS control completes all 30 steps, including CUDA-graph capture, with finite logged losses and gradient norms and zero skipped/NaN iterations.

No convergence settings were relaxed. Existing disabled gradient checks remain unvalidated.
The batch-size correction resolves configuration validity, but additional memory-fit work is needed before the B200 BF16 preset is runnable.

_Drafted with Codex (GPT-6)._

Thanks for running the B200 BF16 retest. I updated the PR description to distinguish the batch-divisibility fix from end-to-end runtime validation. The OOM before graph capture means this preset still needs memory-fit work; I have not changed recompute or parallelism settings without a measured candidate.

Could you share the full OOM diagnostic (requested allocation and free, allocated, and reserved GPU memory), the affected rank's memory near the failure, and confirmation that `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` was active? Those figures would help separate allocator fragmentation from a capacity limit and choose a specific configuration to test through multiple BF16 steps.

Thanks for clarifying the scope. `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` was set on all 256 ranks. The allocator also emitted `expandable_segments` mapping failures, confirming that it was active.
Here is the full OOM diagnostic for rank 6:
```
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 512.00 MiB. GPU 6 has a total capacity of 178.35 GiB of which 119.00 MiB is free. Including non-PyTorch memory, this process has 178.21 GiB memory in use. Of the allocated memory 172.45 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, and 953.90 MiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated.
```
The failing allocation is in `mamba_ssm/ops/triton/ssd_chunk_state.py:826`, in `_chunk_state_fwd`.
Immediately preceding the exception, the same rank reported an expandable-segment mapping failure requesting **20 MiB**, with **19 MiB free**. These figures and the exception’s 119 MiB free are separate observations during the failure sequence.
Rank 6’s recorded allocator peaks were:
- Allocated: **185,161,845,248 bytes (172.4454 GiB)**
- Reserved: **186,245,971,968 bytes (173.4551 GiB)**

Those are high-water marks reported at process exit, not a time-resolved memory snapshot. The exception above provides the memory figures at the failed allocation.
This points to severe capacity pressure even with expandable segments enabled. However, the 953.90 MiB reserved-but-unallocated exceeds the requested allocation, so these figures alone do not rule out fragmentation or allocation-reuse constraints. I would avoid attributing the failure exclusively to either cause without an allocator snapshot.
No recomputation or parallelism candidate has been validated yet; the batch-divisibility fix remains independently supported.
_Drafted with Codex (GPT-6)._

The allocator evidence is now reflected in the PR description. It confirms severe memory pressure with expandable segments active, while the reserved-but-unallocated figure leaves fragmentation or allocation-reuse constraints unresolved. I’m keeping this PR scoped to the independently validated batch-divisibility correction; a recompute or parallelism change needs its own measured 256-GPU BF16 validation through steady-state steps.

The diagnostic supports classifying this as severe capacity pressure rather than a batch-divisibility failure: only 119 MiB was free for a 512 MiB allocation, with 172.45 GiB allocated by PyTorch. Because roughly 954 MiB was reserved but unallocated, fragmentation or allocation-reuse constraints still cannot be excluded without an allocator snapshot. I will keep this PR scoped to the validated GBS correction and leave BF16 preset runtime readiness unresolved until a measured memory-fit candidate completes multiple steps.
